title: Reduce exact downset replay time with integer dot products
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Reduces the full downset proof replay from **19.814 to 16.715 seconds** in a final local comparison, about **16% less time**, by replacing repeated Fraction operations in matrix multiplication with scaled integer dot products. Every original scientific evidence field and rejection-witness count stays equal. This is a verifier runtime improvement; the proof and complete kappa calculation do not change.

[Arithmetic identity and evidence](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/afe5f0d86a51559075320ab392592dea16e8e247/research/downset-block-solve-bound/README.md), [implementation and direct product oracle](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/afe5f0d86a51559075320ab392592dea16e8e247/research/downset-block-solve-bound/verify.py), and [unchanged source pins](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/afe5f0d86a51559075320ab392592dea16e8e247/research/downset-block-solve-bound/SOURCES.json).

Each row of the left matrix and each column of the right matrix is scaled by its denominator LCM. Their dot product uses integers, then one Fraction reduction per output. There is no cache or floating point arithmetic. The valid rectangular rational input contract and fixed matrix capacities are unchanged.

## Task and overlap

Takes the non-caching multiplication follow-up from [PR #4947](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4947). Base: `f259dabc7d70e0db8d6d36bfda888f008bbfecc1`, priority 7. That main-branch file still contains the original inverse algorithm. This PR leaves it unchanged; the timing comparison is against those exact main bytes, not PR #4947's inverse-cache version. The original package metadata and historical provenance pins remain byte-exact.

The final search covered 300 open PRs, 4,098 Discussion records and 69 of 6,710 local notes. It found the separate inverse-cache and Full-allocation work. Sparse omitted notes, arbitrary diffs and unpublished work remain limits.

## Validation

CPython 3.12.13, standard library:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/downset-block-solve-bound
```

Expected: both commands print `PASS_DOWNSET_BLOCK_SOLVE`, followed by `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`. Normal and optimized replay passed. All original counts remain equal: 46 trees, 2,380 states, 9,520 matrix identities, 23,504 spectral certificates, 9,372 partition blocks and eleven original control groups. The added `product_controls: 93` field records signed/zero/rectangular Fraction-oracle comparisons, ownership/type checks and invalid-input controls. Four actual arithmetic mutations fail against that oracle.

Exact source-pin checks, committed-byte checks and Git-free read-only optimized export replay passed. The full-history wrapper was not run in this shallow checkout; all four historical blob/SHA-256 pins were checked directly. No selected cold replay, Lean, Docker or archive-wide sweep ran.

Timing uses sequential full subprocess replays on the same shared macOS host. Two earlier trials measured 19.488/21.431 seconds before and 16.765/16.696 seconds after; the final pair includes the new controls. This is local timing evidence, not a cross-platform guarantee.

## Credit

Nick Petalas supplied the mathematics, fixtures and original checker; see the [original source notice](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/f259dabc7d70e0db8d6d36bfda888f008bbfecc1/research/downset-block-solve-bound/README.md). Brian (JoyboyBrian) identified the remaining product bottleneck in [PR #4947](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4947). Their predecessor credits are retained. Prepared for Ali Romman with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

The effect when combined with the separate inverse-cache implementation has not been measured. Other rational verifiers need their own bottleneck profile and exact equivalence checks before using this change.
